title: General Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: The Board of Directors; Directors and Company Secretary of any subsidiary; any person entitled to receive equity performance rights and/or options under an equity incentive scheme; any Executives (executive officers involved in strategic and operational management, including each Company Secretary); and each Company Secretary of the Company. All substantive rules (blackout, notification/clearance, exceptional-circumstances relief) apply uniformly to this tier.

tiers.name: Associated Parties
tiers.description: Immediate family (including a spouse or equivalent, or dependent), family company or trust of a Restricted Person. Each Restricted Person is personally responsible for ensuring their Associated Parties comply with the same restrictions.

windows.start_anchor: five business days before the announcement of a dividend or any other capital management initiative that might have a material impact on the share price
windows.end_anchor: announcement of the dividend or capital management initiative

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may from time to time designate further periods of time as a prohibited period, and separately the Board has absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons, employees and/or their associated parties trading in the Company's shares at any time. The policy does not state whether the existence or reason for such a designation or embargo is kept confidential.

rules.detail: The policy only regulates 'dealing in shares' and never defines 'Dealing' or 'Securities' to extend to derivatives, options over shares, or other financial products created over shares. No provision names or otherwise catches an OTC put or call.
No hedging concept, definition, or restriction of any kind (including over unvested equity incentive securities) appears anywhere in the policy.
No mention of prepaid forwards, deferred purchase agreements, collars or other monetisation structures; the policy addresses only conventional buying and selling of shares.
CFDs are never mentioned and there is no derivatives or financial-product definition to catch them.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over shares is never mentioned and is not captured by any dealing definition (none exists).
No provision addresses secured or other financing arrangements in respect of the Company's shares.
No minimum holding period, intention test, or restriction on short-term trading appears anywhere in the policy.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary (who confers with the Chairman of the Board)
clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons are required to notify the Company of intended dealings in shares, by themselves or their associated parties, of the Company prior to such intended dealings. ... A Company Secretary will confer with the Chairman of the Board in relation to any proposed dealing.

exceptions.approver: Chairman (or another Director if the Chairman is involved)
exceptions.evidence: the Chairman may, at his discretion but subject to this section 8, give clearance for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) shares in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so ... 'exceptional circumstances' includes severe financial hardship

exceptions.approver: Chairman (or another Director if the Chairman is involved)
exceptions.evidence: 'exceptional circumstances' includes ... a court order (or court enforceable undertaking), or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement, to transfer or sell shares in the Company
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer or pursuant to a scheme of arrangement implemented in accordance with section 411 of the Corporations Act

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the entity) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

the cancellation or surrender of an option under an employee scheme; ... transfer of shares arising out of the operation of an employee scheme into a savings scheme investing only in securities of the Company following the exercise of an option under a savings related share option scheme

where a Restricted Person is a trustee, trading in the securities of the entity by that trust provided the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the restricted person

external_documents: Insider Trading Policy, set out in section 6 of the Corporate Governance Charter
exemption_authority: The Chairman (or another Director, if the Chairman is the one seeking clearance) may, in his discretion, give written clearance for a Restricted Person to sell (but not purchase) shares during an otherwise prohibited period where 'exceptional circumstances' exist (severe financial hardship, a court order or enforceable undertaking, another overriding legal/regulatory requirement to transfer or sell, or other circumstances the Chairman deems exceptional), provided no inside information exists at the time; the Chairman must fix and state the maximum duration of the clearance in writing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to trading in the Company's shares on the ASX ... Restricted Persons ... must restrict their buying and selling of Company's shares.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because the policy never defines 'Dealing' or 'Securities' to extend beyond shares themselves, an OTC put/call and a share pledge to a bank are not expressly named or swept in by any definition, so a funded collar sits in a gap this document does not address rather than being either cleared or barred by it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: external Insider Trading Policy not in scope
bespoke_clauses.clause: In addition to the requirements of this General Trading Policy, all Restricted Persons ... must also comply with the Insider Trading Policy of the Company in section 6 of the Corporate Governance Charter.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The substantive controls on derivatives, hedging, margin lending, encumbrance and secured financing that a typical ASX trading policy contains may instead sit in the externally incorporated Corporate Governance Charter, which is not in this document and must be obtained and reviewed before relying on any 'not_addressed' conclusion here.

bespoke_clauses.clause: give clearance for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) shares in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if a collar were otherwise permitted, the only express relief from a prohibited-period restriction is for an outright share sale, not for entering into a put/call or a security interest, so it gives no comfort for executing collar legs during a blackout.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or employees and/or their respective associated parties trading in the Company's shares at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An ad hoc embargo of unstated duration and confidentiality could freeze entry, roll or unwind of a collar without notice or an available relief route (relief under section 8 is sale-only).

bespoke_clauses.clause: 'associated parties' (being immediate family (including a spouse (or equivalent) or dependent), family company or trust)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because associates are limited to immediate family and family entities, a bank-side special purpose vehicle or nominee used to structure the collar would likely fall outside this definition and outside the policy's reach altogether, absent guidance from the external Insider Trading Policy.

summary: This is a bare-bones share trading policy that regulates only conventional buying and selling of Future Generation Investment Fund's shares; it never defines 'Dealing' or 'Securities' to extend to derivatives, hedging, margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing, so a funded OTC collar (purchased put, written call, and a loan secured on the shares) is not expressly prohibited but is also not expressly permitted or cleared by this document. Any such arrangement would need to be assessed against the externally incorporated Insider Trading Policy in section 6 of the Corporate Governance Charter, which is not part of this text and could contain the substantive derivatives/financing controls this policy lacks. Whatever the answer, execution would still need to clear the five-business-day blackout before dividend or capital management announcements, any ad hoc Board embargo (unlimited, of unstated confidentiality), and the prior notification/clearance process run by the Company Secretary and Chairman, who can refuse clearance. The only express relief from a prohibited period is a Chairman-approved sale (not purchase) in narrowly defined exceptional circumstances such as hardship or a court order, which would not extend to writing options or granting security. Overall, a funded collar is possible only if the (unreviewed) Insider Trading Policy does not itself bar it, and even then only outside blackout/embargo periods and with prior notification to the Company Secretary and Chairman.
